\begin{chapstatus}{The thread of this chapter}
The add of Lecture 02 is now a circuit you could draw: 32 full adders and a carry that ripples. Next: the electronics that make a gate.
\par\medskip\textbf{Exit ticket} (two to four minutes, alone, on paper):
\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=2em]
\item A full adder receives A = 1, B = 1, Cin = 1. Give S and Cout. Why does a 32-bit adder need 32 of them, chained?
\item In a Karnaugh map of three variables A, B, C, why can the cells 000 and 010 be grouped, but not 000 and 011? Which term does the first group give?
\end{enumerate}
\end{chapstatus}
